behavior: Given a pool at its cap whose least-recently-used workspace is being evicted and is still inside its process stop(), when a concurrent acquire for that same project root starts a second JDT LS process under the same workspaceId and that successor absorbs a publishDiagnostics for a URI, then after the predecessor's stop() completes and its eviction cleanup runs, querying that URI under that workspaceId still returns the successor's report and never the explicit 'not reported yet' marker.
rationale: Stateful, not integration: outcome depends on pool history and the scenario runs on a fake spawnWorkspace, not two real components; D2 bars concurrent for a single-threaded event loop. A real JDT LS turns the window into a timing dependency and no command sequence builds it (#ensureCapacityFor awaits all of #evict), so deterministic replay of one scripted overlap fits, invariant checked after. Oracle is unit-level: test/workspace/workspace-succession.spec.ts, not test/integration/ [INV-DIAG-1].
